pool.text: Hobart was established as the seat of government for the southern district of Tasmania.
The northern lieutenant governorship ceased, making Hobart the de facto seat of government.
Hobart officially became the capital of an independent colony of Van Diemen's Land.
Hobart became the seat of responsible self government under the Australian Constitutions Act.
The MV Cartela began operating as one of Australia's oldest still operating vessels.
One of the last known surviving thylacines died at the Beaumaris Zoo.
A short-lived trolleybus network consisting of six routes operated in the city until this year.
Suburban passenger trains run by the Tasmanian Government Railways were closed down.
The intrastate passenger service known as the Tasman Limited ceased running.
Hobart Airport announced plans to receive major upgrades including a first floor and aerobridges.
Sullivans Cove Whiskey won the prestigious award for the world's best single malt.
Freight rail operations ceased within Hobart and the Riverline proposal was scrapped.
Work began on a 500-metre extension and a 100 million dollar airport upgrade.
The Tolosa dam located in Glenorchy was officially disused.
Visitor numbers reached a low primarily as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Greater Hobart was divided into seven local government areas according to the census.
A ferry trial servicing Hobart central business district and Bellerive was initiated.
More ferry terminal sites were revealed across multiple waterfront locations.
St Helen's Private Hospital featuring a mother-baby unit was closed.
A new Tasman private hospital proposed on a former WIN News site was abandoned.
